text: Cece Ma is a Computer Science CO-OP student at the University of Ottawa, expected to graduate in December 2027 with a 3.9/4.0 GPA. She has interned at Intuit, Magnet Forensics, RBC Direct Investing, Remsoft, and the Ontario Government. Her current engineering focus is backend systems, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and observability.

Cece is pursuing an Honours Bachelor of Computer Science at the University of Ottawa, expected graduation December 2027. Her GPA is 3.9/4.0. Coursework includes Data Structures and Algorithms, Networking, and Operating Systems.
Cece's school email is yma178@uottawa.ca. Her LinkedIn is linkedin.com/in/cc-yuqing-ma/ and her GitHub is github.com/ccm32004.

Cece is most interested in backend engineering, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, developer tooling, and observability. She enjoys data pipelines, messaging systems, event-driven architecture, APIs, CI/CD, and making production systems easier to measure, debug, and operate.

From January 2026 to April 2026, Cece was a Software Developer Intern at Intuit in Toronto. She developed Java SDK functionality for Apache Pulsar sources, including Kubernetes Secrets and schema validation for pipelines. She optimized data pipelines with batch processing, reducing latency by 7× and increasing throughput by 125%. She built automated CI benchmarking workflows with Prometheus to detect throughput, latency, and CPU regressions. She also reduced pipeline startup time by 95% by removing Spring Boot dependencies.

From September 2025 to December 2025, Cece was a Software Developer Intern at Magnet Forensics in Waterloo. She built automated LocalStack environments emulating AWS services including S3, SQS, SNS, EC2, and VPC so integration tests could run without real cloud dependencies. She eliminated recurring deployment race conditions by engineering commit-hash based global deployments in Jenkins. She optimized APIs by migrating DynamoDB scan-based access to key prefix queries, reducing lookup time by 92%. She also architected a real-time incident alerting pipeline using CloudWatch and AWS Lambda for automated Slack notifications, cutting incident response time by 30%.

From January 2025 to April 2025, Cece was an iOS Software Developer Intern at RBC Direct Investing in Toronto. She developed and presented trading-screen POCs using MVVM with Swift and SwiftUI. She improved app performance with cached date formatters, reducing memory allocations by 42%. She implemented client usage tracking with RBC's Google Analytics framework and wrote Swift unit and stub tests integrated into CI/CD with Jenkins and GitHub Actions.

From May 2024 to August 2024, Cece was a Mobile Software Developer Intern at Remsoft in Ottawa. She implemented location tracking by integrating native device features such as audio, GPS, and WiFi with Flutter. She enhanced app security with CBC-mode encryption for device licensing and developed custom Kotlin plugins for automatic file parsing, accelerating client business processes by 58%.

From May 2023 to September 2023, Cece was an IT Systems Assistant / Software Developer for the Ontario Government in the Judiciary IT Systems branch in Toronto. She automated data entry for judicial archives with Python and Selenium, increasing speed by 50%. She also implemented user authentication and authorization for a judges app with Entity Framework Core.

From September 2023 to April 2025, Cece was an Avionics Software Developer on uORocketry at the University of Ottawa. She built a real-time health monitoring dashboard for server and hardware systems using Rust and TypeScript, implemented 3D visualization of live rocket telemetry with Svelte and CesiumJS, and optimized GraphQL queries with Hasura to retrieve telemetry data from PostgreSQL.

Cece built her personal website with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, and Framer Motion on the frontend. Its backend is a FastAPI RAG chatbot that uses Pinecone for vector search and Gemini for embeddings and generated answers. The site is hosted on Netlify and the backend on Render. Visitors can ask the chatbot about her experience, projects, skills, and interests.

Cece created MelodyMatch, a full-stack song-guessing game using Spotify API audio snippets. The frontend uses React, Mantine, and Vite; the backend uses Express.js with Redis for streaks and MongoDB for persistent scores. It is containerized with Docker and deployed to AWS EC2 with NGINX. She built it because she loves Taylor Swift and wanted a fun way to test song knowledge.

Cece built an AI-powered wear predictor that ranks how likely she is to wear each clothing item. It uses a random forest regression model trained on comfort, trendiness, and fabric quality, with a Streamlit UI, scikit-learn, and Docker.

Cece's programming languages include Python, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, C++, C#, SQL, Go, and Bash. Python is her favorite because of its readability, versatility, and how quickly she can go from an idea to a working prototype.

Cece has backend and data experience with FastAPI, Express.js, Spring Boot, .NET / Entity Framework Core, Apache Pulsar, Kafka, gRPC, Redis, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, GraphQL, and Hasura. She has worked on APIs, streaming pipelines, messaging systems, schema validation, and data access optimization.

Cece's cloud and DevOps experience includes AWS services such as S3, SQS, SNS, EC2, VPC, DynamoDB, CloudWatch, and Lambda, along with LocalStack, Docker, Kubernetes, Jenkins, NGINX, Azure DevOps, Cloudflare, GitHub Actions, and CI/CD automation.

Cece has used Prometheus, Datadog, and CloudWatch for metrics, monitoring, alerting, incident response, and regression detection. At Intuit she built CI benchmarking to catch throughput, latency, and CPU regressions, and at Magnet Forensics she worked on automated CloudWatch and AWS Lambda incident alerts.

Cece has worked with React, SwiftUI, Flutter, Svelte, scikit-learn, TensorFlow, Tailwind, Framer Motion, and CesiumJS. Her development tools include Git, Jira, Confluence, Postman, Xcode, Claude, and Cursor.

Cece was a Community Organizer for Hack the Hill, coordinating events and logistics for 800+ students. She has also participated in hackathons as a builder, including winning at UOttaHack with Rate My Study Space.

Outside of work and school, Cece enjoys hiking, reading, and pilates. She especially likes forested and challenging hiking trails, scenic places, and the sense of adventure that comes from exploring somewhere new.

Cece enjoys fantasy and stories with morally complex protagonists. One standout favorite is Six of Crows because of its layered characters and clever storytelling. She has also been reading more non-fiction, including Killers of the Flower Moon.
Cece loves sushi, sweets, avocados, and shopping. Her favorite sushi is butterfish sashimi. Some of her favorite stores are Aritzia, Brandy Melville, Garage, and Hollister.

Cece's favorite color is purple. She likes turning everyday interests and annoyances into side projects, such as building a clothing wear predictor and a song-guessing game. She also enjoys exploring new developer tools, libraries, and workflows.

Cece likes software engineering because it combines creativity, logic, and practical impact. She enjoys turning ideas into working tools and is especially drawn to systems that are fast, reliable, observable, and easy for other developers to use.
